blocks.text: 03-OFF / offers Goes here. Structuring product-market fit to scale ad spend, iterating product-level pricing, and incentivizing affiliate networks with high-value guarantees. Not here. • Paid ad structure, testing metrics, and ad account learning phases -> 11-ADC • Sourcing samples from Alibaba and supply chain logistics -> 18-COG

Header. url: rights: public_reference why: Details the exact pricing adjustments and affiliate commission guarantees (the $1,000 baseline offer) required to snowball a TikTok Shop creator network. modules: [OFF] topics: [product-market fit, pricing iteration, affiliate offer mechanics] tier: 3 scope_hint: growth

Topics. product-market fit / solving a specific emotional problem (e.g., anxiety/comfort) rather than a functional one; pricing / rapidly iterating price downwards (e.g., dropping to $69) when the market rejects luxury pricing due to lack of brand track record; affiliate offers / structuring zero-risk offers for new creators (e.g., "$1,000 minimum monthly retainer OR 15-20% commission, whichever is higher, in exchange for 30 pieces of content"). Look for. The explicit zero-risk affiliate offer: Guaranteeing a $1,000 floor for 30 videos (1/day) while offering a 15-20% commission upside. When a video goes viral and generates $5k+ in commissions, the creator is hooked, and the brand transitions the relationship to pure commission. Skip. Broad motivational statements about the Law of Attraction, being homeless, or general "vision." Scope mix. 10% baseline (adjusting price), 90% growth (affiliate offer structures). Volume. ~250 words.

10-MCR / paid social creative Goes here. Creative velocity, repurposing UGC across channels, and leveraging AI for hook generation. Not here. • The exact commission structure paid to the affiliates -> 03-OFF • Whitelisting campaigns and ad account management -> 11-ADC

Header. url: rights: public_reference why: Establishes a radical new benchmark for creative velocity—requiring individual creators to post 5 to 7 times daily and managing over 10,000 creatives a week across the brand. modules: [MCR] topics: [creative velocity, TikTok Shops, AI hook generation, UGC variety] tier: 2 scope_hint: growth

Topics. creative velocity / the quality-through-quantity approach (e.g., 200 creatives per month minimum to scale, pushing towards 10,000/week); UGC variety / dictating 80,000 ways to make content (podcasts, street interviews, family reactions, voiceovers, shocking hooks); AI integration / using ChatGPT/Claude to generate 100+ viral hooks to bring to creator meetings; TikTok Shops / requiring creators to post 5 to 7 pieces of content a day per person to maximize organic reach and affiliate sales. Look for. The volume mandate: To achieve hyper-growth, a brand needs to introduce hundreds of new creatives into the ad account monthly (e.g., the benchmark of 200 new creatives in month 3 unlocking $500k in revenue). The specific UGC formats: street interviews, family first reactions, voiceovers for creators who excel at aesthetics but lack on-camera speaking skills. Skip. Mentions of the Kardashian or JLo endorsements unless tied to a specific ad creative execution. Scope mix. 10% baseline (needing UGC), 90% growth (extreme volume mandates, AI hook generation). Volume. ~300 words.

21-OPS / operations and team Goes here. Building an affiliate army, scaling customer support during hyper-growth, maintaining company culture, and leveraging the founder's vision for recruitment. Not here. • The compensation or commission rates paid to the affiliates -> 03-OFF • The ad campaigns running the whitelisted content -> 11-ADC

Header. url: rights: public_reference why: Explains how to recruit, retain, and manage an external army of 500+ micro-creators by treating them as internal employees and promoting top performers to recruiters. modules: [OPS] topics: [affiliate recruitment, creator management, scaling operations, company culture] tier: 3 scope_hint: baseline

Topics. affiliate recruitment / targeting micro-creators (<10k followers) and passionate customers, leveraging the founder's vision over transactional relationships; creator management / promoting top-performing creators to recruit others, holding quarterly brand trips, treating creators with radical transparency (sharing revenue projections, best/worst performing ads, and inventory levels); scaling operations / the danger of hyper-growth breaking customer support and inventory, requiring the rapid onboarding of external agencies and dozens of reps within a month; company culture / extreme alignment, long hours, and integrating non-traditional roles into product design (e.g., the CFO participating in design calls). Look for. The recruitment funnel: Founder pitches the vision to a micro-creator -> Creator succeeds and makes significant commission -> Creator is paid a small base salary to recruit other creators on behalf of the brand. The transparency protocol: Treating the 500+ external content creators exactly like internal employees by sharing exact stock levels, revenue projections, and ad performance data. Skip. Personal anecdotes about the founder's childhood, dropping out of high school, or selling cars. Scope mix. 100% baseline (recruiting, team building, and operational scaling). Volume. ~350 words.
